citations.claim: First pole_upright violation: theta 0.8076 rad exceeds 0.8 limit at step 35
One step before failure pole already at 0.79985 rad, nearly at limit
Three steps earlier pole at 0.755 rad and rising, controller force 35.8N driving instability

counterfactual.change: Set sensor_noise from 0.0118757 to 0, keeping all other fields and steps (35) identical; noiseless feedback stabilizes so no violation.

explanation: Noisy angle/rate feedback (sensor_noise ~0.012) corrupts state-feedback control: controller applies large erroneous forces (23N at step30, 35N at step32, 54N at step34, 63N at step35) that pump energy instead of damping, so theta grows monotonically 0.68->0.755->0.799->0.807 rad and violates pole_upright. With noise removed the same plant/initial conditions stay balanced, proving noise-induced destabilization is the cause.
vision_note: The pole leans to the right and tips progressively further over from steps 32 to 34 with an orange tip, then at step 35 the tip turns red marking the pole-upright violation. The blue cart stays near the center of the track between the walls throughout, so the failure is the pole falling over rather than the cart driving off track.
